title: Climb Waterslide and Slide
dek: In the week after the 11 Sep new-world build (Sat 09-12 → Wed 09-16), DAU rose 71.1% and daily-peak concurrents 88.5% against the same weekdays a week earlier, after a 34.4% fall the week before. Most of the gain landed Mon–Wed from 09-14; the weekend gain came on 22% fewer impressions.
summary: **Audience.** `DailyActiveUsers` 101,759 → 174,157 a day (+71.1%, 5/5 weekday pairs; week before −34.4%): Sat–Sun +13.9%, Mon 09-14 +68.4%, Tue–Wed +163.8%. DAU was 9.1% of its 688,061 peak on Thu 09-10 and 35.7% on Tue 09-15.

**Reach × conversion.** `UniqueUsersWithImpressions` +22.3% and `EndToEndCVR` 3.24% → 4.54% (+40.2%); `RFYPlayThroughRate` 1.32% → 1.94% (+47.1%). On Sat–Sun impressions were −22.2% and CVR +48.1%; on Tue–Wed impressions +100.8% and CVR +30.7%. Over the five pairs, 38% of the log-change in DAU sits in impressions and 63% in conversion.

**Who came.** New players (Explore `IsNewUser=New`) +97.8%, returning +26.7%. Returning players were −7.0% on the weekend after the build and +91.8% on Tue–Wed. HomeRecommendation supplied 78% of the added new players.

**D1.** `ForwardD1Retention` 11.69% → 12.90% (+10.3%): +1.16pp within sources, −0.08pp from mix. HomeRecommendation +13.5% (z +2.30 against its own day-to-day sd), Friends +1.9% (z +0.38), Search +2.8% (z +0.12).

**Concurrents.** Hourly `ConcurrentPlayers` daily mean peaked at 3,125 on Tue 09-15 (+174.4% on Tue 09-08). The week-on-week ratio climbed from ~0.5× on Thu 09-10 to 0.75× in the 03:00 UTC block of Fri 09-11 — before the 16:42 publish — and stepped again at 10:00 UTC Mon 09-14, six hours before v1722. Today (Sat 09-19, 00:00–08:30 UTC) runs +46.3% above the same slots last Saturday.

**Tutorial and reviews.** `Tutorial_Main_5_ToRaftShop` still converts 87.3% of players from step 4 (86.7% the week before; neighbouring steps 96–100%). Raft-shop scrolling complaints went from 10 of 32 reviews (08-28 → 09-11) to 0 of 12 (09-12 → 09-19).

**Technical.** `ClientCrashRate15m` 0.40% → 0.45% (+11.8%; the week before +15.7%), `ClientFpsP10` −5.8%, errors per DAU −11.0%. New error text on the root place since 09-11: three `[RaceService] RaceClaimCoins` warnings (v1721) and a v1722 save/teleport rejection cluster first seen at 09-15 22:08 UTC.

sections.timeline:
**The 11 Sep build.** A new place, `76865069793948` ('Heaven' in the universe's place list), was saved on 09-10 at 09:48 UTC and published as v2 at 09-11 15:52 and v3 at 16:32; the seven existing sub-places were republished 16:33–16:40 and the root place `139617346573330` as **v1721 at 16:42 UTC**. Roblox's `NEW WORLD` event ran 09-11 19:00 → 09-15 18:00 and the Saturday `ADMIN ABUSE` hour 09-12 17:00–18:00. The spec block 'UPD 10.09' lists: a new world (new speed/stamina requirements on the slide, 7 rafts, 2 limited pets, 3 eggs, 3 trails); 4 new coaches plus a limited Angel coach shown in the new world's lobby; fixes for the raft UI not scrolling (mobile and PC) and for players sometimes not receiving cash; a scripted admin abuse.

**Builds with no spec filed.** **v1722** went to every place 09-14 16:09–16:15 and **v1723** to every place 09-17 18:11–18:18. Their contents are unknown; nothing in this page attributes a feature to them. A `NEW UPDATE` event started 09-17 18:00. The thumbnail set changed on 09-05, 09-06, 09-08 (19:44) and 09-13 (22:01). Engine RCC 739 shipped 09-14 22:07. The error-derived deploy log lists v1719 only from 09-09, five days after its 09-04 publish, so builds here are dated from `place-versions.csv`.

**The build before, and the base rate.** The 03.09 update (root v1719, 09-04 19:12; `NEW UPDATE` 09-03 18:00 → 09-07 17:00) was live through the PRE window. The 07.08, 28.08 and 10.09 spec blocks all carry the same 'new world — 7 rafts, 2 limited pets, 3 eggs, 3 trails' line; the launch table runs the same five-day test on each. At its own clock time, no publish moved concurrents outside the range of ordinary days (z +0.38, −0.80, −0.98).
sections.reach:
**DAU +71.1%** (`DailyActiveUsers` 101,759 → 174,157, 5/5 pairs). The per-pair decomposition splits it into impressions × `EndToEndCVR`: on Sat 09-12 and Sun 09-13 impressions were −22.0% and −22.3% while CVR was +40.1% and +56.7%; on Mon–Wed impressions were +18.0%, +126.5% and +74.2% and CVR +45.0%, +35.3% and +26.3%. The impressions change sits in `HomeRecommendation` (+29.6% for the week; −25.2% on the weekend, +126.3% on Tue–Wed); Search impressions were −13.1%.

**Conversion at matched reach.** On this game, conversion and impressions rose and fell together over 08-10 → 09-08 (log–log r +0.71 for CVR), so each post day is set beside pre-period days with impressions within ±15% rather than a fitted line. `RFYPlayThroughRate` on 09-12, 09-13, 09-14, 09-16 and 09-17 sits above every matched pre-period day, and its 09-11 (2.44%) and 09-12 (2.21%) values exceed the pre-period's highest single day (1.97%). PTR first rose on 09-09 (1.63%) and 09-10 (1.74%), the two lowest-impression days of the window (2.03M, 1.42M). In the thumbnail event study the 09-08 19:44 set is followed by a +34.4% day-after/day-before change in PTR (z +2.47 against 60 non-swap days); across all 24 swap days since 06-01 the mean change is −2.8% (z −0.32).

**Who arrived.** New players (`UniqueUsersWithPlaySessions`, `IsNewUser=New`) went from 62,701 to 124,422 a day; HomeRecommendation supplied 78% of the increase and its share of new players went from 63.3% to 70.7%; Search new players fell 12.7%. By country the largest shares of the DAU increase are Indonesia (20.9%, +111.1%), the Philippines (+124.5%), Mexico (+117.2%) and Vietnam (+89.2%); the US was +44.8% and Russia −14.0%. On Tue 09-15, all 15 of the largest countries were above Tue 09-08 (+26.0% to +348.6%).

**Portfolio.** Brainrot also rose this week (DAU +37.3%, impressions +29.2%); Banana Monkey, Verity and Seal fell 40–59% on DAU.
sections.ccu:
`PeakConcurrentPlayers` (daily) 2,049 → 3,864 (+88.5%). The hourly `ConcurrentPlayers` daily mean was 892 on Thu 09-10, 2,133 and 2,158 over the weekend, 3,125 on Tue 09-15 (+174.4% week on week) and 1,981 on Fri 09-18 (+59.5%).

**When it moved.** In the 3-hour-block table the week-on-week ratio sits at 0.44–0.53× all day on Thu 09-10, reaches 0.75× in the 03:00–05:30 UTC block of Fri 09-11 — more than 11 hours before the 16:42 publish — and 0.98× by 21:00, then holds ~1.2× through the weekend. Against the day before, Fri 09-11 ran 1.23–1.55× Thursday from the 03:00 block on; the same Thursday→Friday comparison on 08-28, 09-04 and 09-18 stays within 0.61–1.16×. On Mon 09-14 the half-hour peak went from 1,441 at 09:30 to 2,130 at 10:00 UTC and 3,409 at 12:00 (1.31× → 1.66× → 2.15× Mon 09-07); the late-morning ramp that day was the steepest of 22 days on Waterslide (z +4.90) and, at a smaller size, on Brainrot (z +2.32). The ratio then ran 2.1–3.2× through Thu 09-17, with no break at the `NEW WORLD` event's end (09-15 18:00), and eased to 1.2–1.9× on Fri 09-18.

**Today, partial.** Over the 18 half-hours that had fully elapsed at the 09:01Z pull, Sat 09-19 is +46.3% above Sat 09-12 and +81.6% above Sat 09-05. The Saturday admin-abuse hour (17:00) is outside those slots; a `NEW UPDATE` event has run since 09-17 18:00.
sections.retention:
`ForwardD1Retention` 11.69% → 12.90% (+10.3%, 5/5 pairs; week before −7.1%). By part of the week: Sat–Sun +2.0%, Mon +23.1%, Tue–Wed +12.6%. The Mon base day (09-07, 10.84%) is the lowest of the four Mondays in view. Weighting by new players per source, the blended change is +1.16pp, of which −0.08pp is mix and +1.16pp is within-source.

**By source.** HomeRecommendation 11.30% → 12.82% (+13.5%, z +2.30 against its own daily sd); Others +9.5% (z +1.53); Friends 15.90% → 16.21% (+1.9%, z +0.38); Search 11.29% → 11.61% (+2.8%, z +0.12). By platform: Computer +18.6%, Tablet +15.2%, Phone +7.9%, Console −0.7%. D1 is **unavailable** by `IsNewUser`: the Explore engine rejects that breakdown for `ForwardD1Retention`.

**Return loop.** Returning players (`IsNewUser=Returning`) were −7.0% on Sat–Sun, +10.9% on Mon and +91.8% on Tue–Wed. In the cohort model (seven days of new players × the late-August day-k retention curve), players outside those recent cohorts were 27,665 and 28,163 on the weekend after the build against 28,430 and 27,119 a week earlier, and 27,948 on Tue 09-15 against 13,051. `RFYD2To7PlayDays` −2.0% (week before −7.1%); `RFYD8To28PlayDays` −17.4%, a series that fell on all three other games that serve it (−32.4% to −63.9%). `ForwardD7Retention` has no settled day in the post window (newest 09-10).
sections.engagement:
`AverageSessionLengthMinutes` 14.34 → 14.81 (+3.3%). In the Explore split, new players went 13.94 → 14.51 min and returning 14.88 → 15.45; the within-segment change is +4.0% and the shift toward new players −0.7%. `AveragePlayTimeMinutesPerDAU` −1.6%: returning +3.3%, new −0.2%, with the new-player share of DAU at 61.3% → 71.2% (mix −2.2%, within +1.3%). By platform, session length was +3.5% to +3.9% on Computer, Phone and Tablet and −1.6% on Console.

First-play signals: `RFYDuration0To60` (bounce under 60 s) 12.16% → 10.76% (−11.6%), `RFYDuration61To180` −0.4%, `RFYD1Playtime` +0.7%, `RFYD1QualifiedPlaySessions` −6.6%, `RFYD1CoplayDays` −2.1%. In the daily signal table, bounce under 60 s was 11.4–12.7% on 09-03 → 09-11 and 10.4–11.3% from 09-12.
sections.money:
`DailyRevenue` +47.9% (R$56,322 → R$83,297 a day) on DAU +71.1%. `PayingUsers` 2,660 → 4,181 (+57.2%); `PayingUsersCVR` 2.55% → 2.46% (−3.3%); `AverageRevenuePerPayingUser` R$20.98 → R$19.93 (−5.0%); `AverageRevenuePerUser` −8.7%. By part of the week, revenue moved with DAU on Tue–Wed (+160.8% against +163.8%) and less than DAU on Sat–Sun (+4.6% against +13.9%) and Mon (+28.8% against +68.4%).

By source, DevProduct +50.5% and GamePass +34.0%. `PayingUsersCVR` by platform: Phone −12.9%, Tablet +9.2%, Computer +5.7%. At matched DAU, payers on the five post days sit between −18.5% and +20.9% of the closest-DAU earlier day. Per concurrent-player-hour, DevProduct revenue was R$1.02–1.44 on 09-11 → 09-18 against R$0.97–1.65 on 09-04 → 09-10; in the 24 hours either side of v1723 it was 1.16 → 1.19 (GamePass 0.16 → 0.15). v1723's daily money metrics are not served yet.
sections.funnels:
One funnel is instrumented: `TutorialFunnel`, 15 steps, cohort completion at ONE_DAY. Cumulative completion rose 0.3–1.4pp at every step from 3 to 15 (step 15 `AddFriendTip` 48.1% → 48.7%); the week before it fell 0.4pp at steps 3–4 and 1.7–2.6pp at steps 5–15.

**Step by step.** `Tutorial_Main_5_ToRaftShop` converts 87.3% of the players who reach step 4 (86.7% the week before, 88.2% two weeks before) and `Tutorial_Main_10_BuyEgg` 86.5% (85.8%), against 96–100% for nine of the other twelve steps. By cohort day, step 4 → 5 ran 85.6–89.1% for the cohorts after the 09-11 16:42 publish and 85.8–87.5% for 09-03 → 09-10. The 10.09 spec lists the raft UI not scrolling (mobile and PC) as fixed.

**Maturity.** POST cohorts were first read at a mean age of 3.4 days and PRE at 1.1 days, which favours POST. Read both on 09-19 (PRE older) the change at step 5 is +0.8pp, and with PRE read on 09-14 (closest to age-matched) it is +0.8pp; steps 10, 12 and 15 keep their sign under all three reads.
sections.technical:
`ClientCrashRate15m` 0.40% → 0.45% (+11.8%; week before +15.7%). By day it was 0.36% on 09-05, 0.43% on 09-08 → 09-10, 0.41–0.48% on 09-11 → 09-17 and 0.37% on 09-18. `ClientFpsP10` −5.8% on five pairs and −4.8% on the four clean pairs; its daily mean was 34.13 on 09-05 → 09-10 and 32.31 on 09-11 → 09-18 (Phone −4.6%, Tablet −6.8%, Computer −4.0%). On the same clean pairs FPS p10 was −5.0% on Brainrot and −6.7% on Seal and +4.8% on Banana Monkey. Across 08-22 → 09-17, corr(log DAU, FPS p10) = −0.28.

`ClientMemoryUsagePercentageAvg` −1.4%; OOM exits per 1k DAU +8.0% (five pairs) and +14.9% (four clean pairs). Server side: `ServerFrameRateP10` +2.4%, `MemoryUsageAvg` −16.1%, `CpuTimeAvg` −6.6%. Waterslide's 09-08 FPS point is −2.7% on 09-07, outside the −78% to −88% collapse the other four games show that day (F28).
sections.errors:
**Volume.** `ErrorCount` per DAU 20.08 → 17.86 (−11.0%, 4 pairs; 09-08 is not served). Client errors per DAU 13.95 → 12.81 (−8.1%), server 6.13 → 5.05 (−17.7%). Server errors per DAU on the publish days (09-11 4.73, 09-14 4.20, 09-17 5.07) sit inside the 3.89–8.90 range of the other days in the table.

**What is new since 11 Sep (root place only).** Four exports were pulled today, each capped at 25 rows; the new world's place `76865069793948` is in none of them. New text: `[RaceService] RaceClaimCoins: no active session` (2,594 in 7 days; 2.22 per 1k DAU per day), `calculated grant is 0` (514; 0.44) and `endPos not set … RaceEndClimb may not have been received` (454; 0.39), first seen 09-11 17:37 → 09-12 11:28 UTC, on the cash claim at the end of a slide run. At v1722 a cluster first seen together at 09-15 22:08–22:10 UTC: `SavePlayerData` 502 'Access forbidden' rejections (224 first attempts, 207 third attempts), `DataStore read failed` (76) and `TeleportService:Not allowed` (76).

**Re-filed long-standing text.** The shop price lookup (`GetDeveloperProductInfo` network failures: DnsResolve, Timedout, ConnectFail, TLS, 503) is filed under v1723 from 18:20 UTC, nine minutes after the publish, with the same call path at `ProductMgr` line 133 instead of 125 and one new caller in `GoShop_Raft.setSpeedDisplay`; for the three reasons in both exports it ran 24.0 per 1k DAU per day on 09-10/11 and 37.2 after v1723 (both floors). The raft shop's `GoShop_Raft:102` nil index on open (1,263; five earlier exports) and the server tick's `CopyTableScript:5` via `GamePassMgr.GetData` (4,442; three earlier exports) carry on. The loudest standing rows — sound assets 'not approved for the requester', WaitForChild, the 64-track animation cap, mesh fetches — all appear in the 09-11 export too, and ten of the twelve are lower per 1k DAU.
sections.sentiment:
44 reviews since 08-28 (29 since 09-04) — too few to rate a build on. By theme (regex counts): raft/slide-shop scrolling 10 of 32 reviews on 08-28 → 09-11 (v1715–v1719) and 0 of 12 on 09-12 → 09-19 (v1721–v1723), a split with probability 0.026 if the rate had not changed; progress, items or purchases lost 3 of 32 before and 4 of 12 after, all downvotes; cash not received after a run 1 before, 0 after; other bugs or glitches 6 before, 2 after. The one scrolling complaint after the build is about the dance list, not the raft shop.

Downvote share by build: v1719 44% (16 reviews), v1721 50% (4), v1722 50% (6), v1723 0% (2). Mobile (Phone + Tablet) wrote 27 of the 29 reviews since 09-04 (11 downvotes); Computer 2 (2 downvotes). `PlayerFeedbackVotesCount` (up − down) +72.7%, alongside DAU +71.1%.
sections.method:
- **Multi-place universe.** Eight places. Performance series are Place-filtered unions and the builder takes the widest place set per date; that set includes the new place, which has sessions only from 09-11, so technical rates after that date include the new world's sessions.
- **Error exports are root-place only** (`--place 139617346573330`); errors thrown inside any world place, including the new one, are not in them. All four lists hit the 25-row cap.
- **Hourly CCU.** On 09-19 the hourly bucket labelled 10:00 was still changing between the 09:01Z and 09:11Z pulls (3,169.9 → 3,180.6), so every 09-19 bucket from 09:00 is dropped; half-hour slots are compared only if fully elapsed.
- **Conversion vs reach.** Over 08-10 → 09-08 this game's conversion rose with impressions (log–log r +0.71 for CVR), the opposite of the inverse relation measured on other games, so matched-reach comparisons use impression bands, not a fit.
- **Events on both sides.** PRE carries `NEW UPDATE` (09-03 → 09-07) and ADMIN ABUSE 09-05; POST carries `NEW WORLD` (09-11 → 09-15) and ADMIN ABUSE 09-12. Mon 09-07, the base for Mon 09-14, was the US Labor Day holiday.
- **Funnel capture ages** are computed from each point's `capturedAt` and from the 09-14 and 09-19 raw bundles; the builder's own capture-age field is empty for funnels.
- **Money.** The corpus copy of `ItemMonetizationRevenue` carries 20×-scale restatements, so the hourly revenue here is read from the single 09-19 raw bundle; its daily sums match `DailyRevenue` at 1.00–1.01.
- **Lags.** Behavioural series end 09-17 (D1 09-16); CCU, crash and errors reach 09-18/19. Nothing behavioural is graded for v1723.
- **Controls.** Brainrot rose this week too, so it is a co-mover here rather than a flat floor. D1 cannot be split by `IsNewUser` (rejected by Roblox), so new/returning mix is tested on session and playtime, and source mix on D1.
sections.diagnosis: Any explanation has to cover a pattern in three parts. **First**, conversion moved before the build: `RFYPlayThroughRate` rose from 09-09 and the concurrents ratio turned from ~03:00 UTC on 09-11, both before the 16:42 publish. **Second**, the weekend after the build gained players on conversion alone — impressions −22%, returning players −7%. **Third**, a Home reach step from 10:00 UTC on Mon 09-14, six hours before v1722, carried the Tue–Wed peak. Two earlier new-world launches with the same spec line were each followed by DAU falls (−48.0%, −33.6%). The hypotheses are ordered by how much of that pattern each explains; several are ruled out or weakened, and those negatives are part of the result.

hypotheses.title: A Home-recommendation reach step from Mon 09-14 carried the Tue–Wed peak
hypotheses.claim: Most of the week's volume is a Home reach expansion that began around 10:00 UTC on Monday 09-14; what triggered it is not identified.
for: Home impressions +27.4% on Mon and +126.3% on Tue–Wed; on the Tue and Wed pairs 71–72% of the DAU log-change sits in impressions.
The Monday late-morning CCU ramp was the steepest of 22 days (z +4.90), starting in the 10:00 half-hour, six hours before v1722 (16:09).
HomeRecommendation supplied 78% of the added new players (+121.6%); returning players were −7.0% on the weekend, +10.9% on Mon and +91.8% on Tue–Wed.
Growth skews to Indonesia, the Philippines, Mexico, Vietnam, Malaysia and Thailand (+89% to +125%) against the US (+44.8%); every top-15 country rose on Tue 09-15.
against: It does not explain the weekend: impressions were −22.2% on Sat–Sun while DAU rose 13.9%.
Brainrot's ramp that morning was also its steepest of 22 days (z +2.32), so a platform-side Home refresh and a game-specific push cannot be separated.

Before 09-14 no ranking signal except play-through moved: D2–7 play days 0.24–0.27 and bounce 11.4–12.7% on 09-03 → 09-11. Competitive displacement or a recommender change cannot be tested from one universe.
hypotheses.test: Home impressions and new players by source for 09-17 → 09-20 (served 09-19 → 09-22): a return to the pre-09-14 level with PTR holding means a transient push; a hold means the game re-ranked. The D7 of the 09-15/16 cohorts (readable ~09-24/25) says whether the arrivals stayed.
hypotheses.lever: Distribution response, not a product defect: the lever is keeping the arrivals (D1 → D7 of the 09-14 → 09-16 cohorts), since Home ranks on per-user return signals.

hypotheses.title: The listing converted better before the build — the 09-08 thumbnail set
hypotheses.claim: The first leg — play-through rising from 09-09 and concurrents turning before the 16:42 publish on 09-11 — lines up with the thumbnail set changed on 09-08 at 19:44.
for: PTR day after vs day before the 09-08 swap: +34.4% (z +2.47 against 60 non-swap days); PTR 1.63% on 09-09, 1.74% on 09-10, 2.44% on 09-11.

PTR on 09-11 and 09-12 exceeds the pre-period's highest day (1.97%), and on 09-12/13/14/16/17 exceeds every pre-period day at matched reach; Home conversion 4.81–4.90% on the weekend against 2.91–4.67% at matched reach.
The CCU ratio turned in the 03:00–05:30 UTC block of 09-11, at least 10 hours before the first publish that day (the new place, 15:52).
D1 rose in HomeRecommendation (+13.5%) and not among Friends (+1.9%), the channel that never sees a thumbnail — the shape a better-matched listing audience would give.
against: Swaps usually do nothing here: the mean over all 24 swap days since 06-01 is −2.8% (z −0.32), and one swap reaching z +2.47 among 24 happens by chance with probability 0.15 — and this date was picked because it preceded the rise.
Impressions fell 21.6% across the same days, and 09-09/10 were the lowest-reach days of the window.
The 09-05 swap was followed by −24.3% and the 09-13 swap by −18.0%; the images themselves were not inspected.
hypotheses.test: The per-thumbnail click and play-through figures in the Creator Dashboard's thumbnail view for the 09-05, 09-08 and 09-13 sets — readable now. A reverted A/B of the 09-08 winner would settle it causally.
hypotheses.lever: Creative: keep the winning image of the 09-08 set in rotation and test against it.

hypotheses.title: The shift toward new players and Home/SEA traffic moved the per-player averages
hypotheses.claim: The new-player share rising from 61.3% to 71.2% accounts for the fall in playtime per DAU and part of the fall in ARPDAU, but not for the D1 rise.
for: Playtime per DAU: mix effect −2.2% against a within-segment +1.3%.
ARPDAU −8.7% with payer CVR −3.3%; Phone payer CVR −12.9% while Tablet +9.2% and Computer +5.7%; growth concentrated in lower-spend markets (Indonesia, the Philippines, Vietnam).
Revenue lagged DAU on the weekend and Monday (+4.6%, +28.8%) and matched it on Tue–Wed.
against: D1: mix −0.08pp, within-source +1.16pp — the D1 rise is not composition by source.
Session length rose within both segments (+4.1% new, +3.9% returning).
At matched DAU, payers sit between −18.5% and +20.9% of earlier days, with no consistent sign.

Against the portfolio, payer conversion ROSE (index 1.15–1.42 from 11 Sep) while spend per payer fell (ARPPU 0.79–0.91): the ARPDAU softness sits in spend per payer, not in fewer paying players (*against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep* (At a glance)).
hypotheses.test: `AverageRevenuePerUser` and `PayingUsersCVR` by `IsNewUser` and by `Country` (not pulled); readable from the next Explore pull.
hypotheses.lever: Monetisation of first-day players and regional price points, measured on payer CVR by segment.

hypotheses.title: The 11 Sep new-world content lifted the game
hypotheses.claim: The new world did not start the volume rise — Waterslide was already shrinking less than the portfolio before the build — but its rates improved against the rest of the portfolio from the build weekend, which is what better content would do and what a shift toward new players would not.
for: Against the other four games (*against the other four games, day by day from 08 Sep* (At a glance)): D1 1.13–1.16 from 12 Sep against 1.00–1.07 before; `PayingUsersCVR` 1.15–1.42 from 11 Sep against 0.96–1.10 on 08–10 Sep. Both rise while the new-player share rises (61.3% → 71.2%), and new players retain and pay worse — so mix pushes these rates the other way.
The CCU ratio climbed 0.86× → 0.98× through the evening of 09-11 after the 16:42 publish and 19:00 event start.
Session length +4.0% within segment and bounce under 60 s −11.6% in the post week.
against: The DAU index was already 1.24–1.81 against the portfolio on 08–11 Sep, before the build: the volume turn is not the build's.
The turn began in the 03:00–05:30 UTC block of 09-11, at least 10 hours before the first 09-11 publish (15:52) — Friday vs Thursday 1.38× against 0.61–1.16× on other Fridays.
The 08-07 and 08-28 launches, same spec line, were followed by DAU −48.0% and −33.6% on the same five-day test.
Returning players, the ones who could go to a new world, were −7.0% on the weekend after; players outside the recent cohorts were 27,665 and 28,163 against 28,430 and 27,119 a week earlier.
The publish-hour event study sits inside ordinary days (z +0.38); DevProduct revenue per CCU-hour did not step up with the new paid items (1.44 and 1.30 on the weekend against 1.58 and 1.37).
hypotheses.test: Concurrents and funnel-style progress inside the new place `76865069793948` (a Place-scoped CCU/crash pull, or a world-progress funnel) — not in this data. Readable on the next grab if requested with that place as the only filter.
hypotheses.lever: Content alone did not move this game on two of three launches; pair new worlds with the return-loop and listing work.

hypotheses.title: v1722 (Mon 09-14 16:09, contents unknown) set off the Monday step
hypotheses.claim: The Monday rise began about six hours before v1722 was published, so v1722 did not start it; what v1722 did afterwards is unknown.
for: Tue–Wed, after v1722, carried the largest gains (DAU +163.8%, D1 +12.6%).
against: The half-hour peak went 1,441 → 2,130 between 09:30 and 10:00 UTC on 09-14; v1722 went out at 16:09.
The publish-hour event study for v1722 sits inside ordinary days (z −0.80).
No spec is filed, so no feature can be tied to it.
hypotheses.test: The v1722 spec from the studio; D1 for the 09-15 → 09-17 cohorts against 09-12 → 09-14 once settled (09-19 → 09-20).

hypotheses.title: Lifecycle decay continues underneath the push
hypotheses.claim: The game sits on a decay curve (9.1% of peak on 09-10); the push lifted it to 35.7% on 09-15 and the ratio is already easing, which is what a pulse on a decaying base looks like.
for: Daily CCU mean 3,125 on 09-15, then 2,619, 1,976 and 1,981 on 09-16 → 09-18; the week-on-week ratio eased from 2.1–2.5× on 09-16/17 to 1.2–1.9× on 09-18.
`RFYD8To28PlayDays` −17.4% (week before −6.3%); `MonthlyActiveUsers` −12.1%.
The week before the build, DAU was −34.4% and CCU −34.7%.
against: Today's settled slots run +46.3% above last Saturday, so the post-push level has not returned to the pre-build one.
D8–28 play days fell on all three other games that serve the series, so part of that fall is not specific to Waterslide.
hypotheses.test: The week of 09-19 → 09-23 against 09-12 → 09-16 (readable ~09-25): a return below the 09-05 → 09-09 level means the push was fully transient.

hypotheses.title: Platform-wide or seasonal movement
hypotheses.claim: A platform or calendar effect is not the main story, but Brainrot moved with Waterslide this week and the two cannot be separated with portfolio data alone.
for: Brainrot DAU +37.3% and impressions +29.2%, with its steepest Monday ramp of 22 days on 09-14.
FPS p10 −5.0% on Brainrot and −6.7% on Seal over the same clean pairs; `RFYD8To28PlayDays` fell on all four games that serve it.
Engine RCC 739 shipped 09-14 22:07; the base Monday 09-07 was a US holiday.
against: Banana Monkey, Verity and Seal fell 40–59% on DAU the same week.
Waterslide's Monday ramp (z +4.90) is twice Brainrot's (z +2.32); the other three sit at z +1.52 or below.
hypotheses.test: The same week on titles outside the portfolio in the same genre (not held).

hypotheses.title: The raft-UI scroll fix reached the tutorial's raft-shop step
hypotheses.claim: Raft-shop scrolling complaints stopped after the build, but the tutorial's raft-shop step did not move, so that step's loss is either a different mechanism or not reached by the fix.
for: Raft-shop scrolling complaints: 10 of 32 reviews before, 0 of 12 after (probability 0.026 if unchanged).
Step 4 → 5 was 85.6–89.1% for post-build cohorts against 85.8–87.5% for 09-03 → 09-10 — a small rise.
against: `Tutorial_Main_5_ToRaftShop` step conversion 86.7% → 87.3% (+0.6pp), against 96–100% for the neighbouring steps; the same sign and size under all three maturity reads.
`GoShop_Raft:102: attempt to index nil with 'Get'` in `RefreshList` on open still logs at v1721 (1,263 in 7 days; the same text as five earlier exports).
Review n is small (12 after the build).
hypotheses.test: Read the tutorial's raft-shop path at v1723 (the `CanvasPosition` loop recorded 2026-08-23); step 4 → 5 for the 09-18/19 cohorts, readable 09-20/21.
hypotheses.lever: If the tutorial path is untouched: the tutorial raft-shop step, where ~13% of players who reach step 4 stop.

hypotheses.title: The new world made the client heavier
hypotheses.claim: Frame rate fell about 5% from 09-11 and crash rate is a few hundredths of a point higher; a heavier world is one reading, but the same frame-rate fall shows on two other games and the crash rise started before the build.
for: `ClientFpsP10` daily mean 34.13 → 32.31 from 09-11, Tablet −6.8%, Phone −4.6%, Computer −4.0%.
OOM exits per 1k DAU +8.0% (five pairs), +14.9% (clean pairs); crash rate 0.41% → 0.44% (daily means).
against: Crash rate was already 0.36% → 0.43% between 09-05 and 09-08 → 09-10, before the build (+15.7% the week before).
FPS p10 fell 5.0% on Brainrot and 6.7% on Seal on the same clean pairs.
Client memory −1.4%; session length +4.0% within segment. A performance loss would also remove its own victims from these averages, so its cost cannot be sized here.
hypotheses.test: `ClientFpsP10`, `ClientCrashRate15m` and `OomUnexpectedExits` with the new place `76865069793948` as the only Place filter, against the other world places (not pulled).
hypotheses.lever: An optimisation budget for the new world, if its own place reads worse.

hypotheses.title: The new error text at v1721/v1722 cost players (cash claims, saves, teleports)
hypotheses.claim: The new `RaceClaimCoins` warnings and the v1722 save/teleport rejections are real but small, and no rate on their surfaces moved the wrong way.
for: `RaceClaimCoins` 'no active session' / 'grant is 0' / 'endPos not set' are new text at v1721 (2.22, 0.44, 0.39 per 1k DAU per day) on the cash-claim path the spec says was fixed.
207 third-attempt `SavePlayerData` failures ('Access forbidden') from 09-15 22:08 UTC; progress-loss reviews: 4 of 12 after the build.
against: Session length +4.0% and playtime +1.3% within segment, D1 +10.3% — the rates a failed cash claim would depress did not fall.
Progress-loss reviews were 3 of 32 before the build as well; v1719 logged `SavePlayerData` failures too (with an 'internal error' reason).
Counts are floors from capped, root-only lists; the errors' unit is undocumented.
hypotheses.test: Read `RaceService.RaceClaimCoins` and the `SaveLoadDataMgr` retry path at v1723 to learn whether a warning means an unpaid run or a lost save; watch the 'Access forbidden' rows in a v1723 export.
hypotheses.lever: If a warning is an unpaid run or an unsaved session: a retry/queue on that path, measured on playtime per DAU and progress-loss reviews.

hypotheses.title: v1723 broke the shop's price lookups
hypotheses.claim: Shop price-lookup failures per player roughly rose after v1723 and gained a raft-shop caller, but the failure text is a network condition and no money signal has moved yet.
for: `GetDeveloperProductInfo` failures, three shared reasons: 24.0 → 37.2 per 1k DAU per day (both floors); first seen nine minutes after the 18:11 publish; a new call from `GoShop_Raft.setSpeedDisplay`.
against: The same messages have logged since June; the reasons (DnsResolve, Timedout, ConnectFail, TLS) are client-network conditions.
DevProduct revenue per CCU-hour 1.16 → 1.19 in the 24 hours either side of v1723; GamePass 0.16 → 0.15.
hypotheses.test: ARPDAU and payer CVR for 09-18 and 09-19 (served 09-20 → 09-21) against the same weekdays; and whether the raft shop shows a price when the lookup fails (code read).
hypotheses.lever: If prices or purchase buttons hang on a failed lookup: cache prices and fall back, measured on payer CVR.

hypotheses.title: Events (NEW WORLD, admin abuse, RSVPs) carried the volume
hypotheses.claim: The event calendar does not account for the volume.
for: `NEW WORLD` ran 09-11 19:00 → 09-15 18:00, across the rise; RSVPs +1,937 and +1,925 on 09-11/12.
against: RSVP increments of at most ~2,000 a day sit beside a DAU change of +14,121 on the day after launch (appendix table) and much larger ones from 09-14.
The same event type on 08-07 and 08-28 preceded falls; CCU showed no break at the event's end (18:00 block 3.11×, 21:00 3.10× on 09-15).
Both comparison Saturdays carry an ADMIN ABUSE hour, and it sits outside the matched slots read today.

reads.what: DAU, revenue, payers and impressions for Fri 09-18 — the first full day on v1723 (published 09-17 18:11). D1 for the 09-17 cohort (publish day, mixed).
D1 for the 09-18 cohort (first clean v1723 cohort); ARPDAU for 09-19; tutorial step 4 → 5 for 09-18/19 cohorts at 2+ days' age.
Whether Home impressions for 09-17 → 09-19 hold above the pre-09-14 level or fall back (the reach-step test).
`ForwardD7Retention` for the 09-15/16 cohorts — whether the players from the reach step came back.
The full week 09-19 → 09-23 against 09-12 → 09-16: whether the push was transient.
